note: Machine-readable classification of every readiness-model gate and every open P1. Harm answers are data. Rescoping moves an obligation; it never deletes one. validate-readiness.py is authority for scores; hand-typed mirrors in readiness.json are checked for drift.

soak_rederivation.derivation: 2 × pgxpool MaxConnLifetime (1800s) so a live connection-pool recycle is observed with samples on both sides. 24h is not the unique observation window for any soak assertion; see docs/BACKEND_ALPHA_CONTRACT.md §6.
examined_and_not_24h_only: executionEnvelopeMaxTTL is a max; min TTL 30s

ALPHA_ENGINEERING_READY.definition: The backend is ready to begin the backend alpha. Synthetic or operator-controlled participants are permitted.
ALPHA_ENGINEERING_READY.blocked_by: every ALPHA_BLOCKER gate plus containment (no live money, no public signup, P0 independent-supplier prohibition in force)

EXTERNAL_ALPHA_PROVEN.definition: A controlled external buyer and a controlled external supplier have actually used the deployed backend.
EXTERNAL_ALPHA_PROVEN.structural_rule: A synthetic, disposable, harness, operator-owned, or operator-controlled identity cannot appear in the receipt. P1-CANARY-REHEARSAL cannot flip this claim. The receipt must carry per-supplier P0 expansion fields; the general P0 prohibition stays listed.

prior_art.source: prior-gate-calibration.patch (unvalidated; scoped to Level B, not backend alpha)
agreed_independently: privacy-qualified-approval is not an alpha start-gate (they said Level C; we say PUBLIC_LAUNCH)
licensing-provenance-approval is not an alpha start-gate (they said Level C; we say PUBLIC_LAUNCH)
staffed-abuse-route-or-tabletop is not an alpha start-gate (they said Level C; we say PUBLIC_LAUNCH)
staffed alert acknowledgement route is not an alpha start-gate (they said Level C; we say PUBLIC_LAUNCH)
P1-STAGING and P1-STRIPE-TEST remain blockers of the thing actually being shipped
disagreed: offsite-backup-verification and offsite-independent-restore: they scoped to Level C because synthetics can be re-seeded. Recovery is in this alpha's purpose and a one-box wipe is reachable; both stay ALPHA_BLOCKER.
qualifying-soak-24h: they kept it as a Level B duration bar. We keep it as the Level B bar (POST_ALPHA from this alpha) and re-derive 3600s for backend alpha.
Their Level B score change (84/100 → 84/94, P1 8→4) is not applied. This lane adds a level; it does not weaken Level B.

gates.harm: Running an unsigned or unverified registry image, so the binary on the persistent plane is not the candidate the operator thinks it is.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: A wrong digest on the droplet executes the wrong control plane against real staging state; this alpha deploys a real image, so the harm is reachable and the receipt is a start-gate.

gates.harm: Shipping an image with no SBOM, signature, or attestation, so a compromise or license-contaminated binary cannot be reconstructed or refused.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The alpha runs a real control-plane image; without a signed SBOM you cannot say what executed or refuse a substituted digest.

gates.harm: An unclassified route silently defaults to an unreviewed allow, so a caller reaches a money, job, or tenant API the matrix never considered.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Allowlisted participants do not make an unclassified route safe; a missing matrix row is a reachable authz hole on the deployed plane.

gates.harm: Cross-tenant read or write, anonymous job submit, or revoked credentials still accepted — buyer input or ledger effects leak or mutate.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Default-deny and the 126-route role matrix are the control that stops one allowlisted participant (or an anonymous caller on a public IP) from reading another tenant's jobs or moving test-mode money.

gates.harm: Emergency access that is unaudited or that cannot recover from operator lockout, so a lockout becomes a permanent outage or a silent god-mode.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The supervising operator can lock themselves out of the persistent plane; unaudited break-glass is a reachable integrity hole, not a later org concern.

gates.harm: A hostile internet user finds an authz or cross-tenant hole on an advertised public TLS staging hostname.
gates.smaller_control: The default-deny authorization matrix and the local technical tabletop cover in-process authz. They do not exercise a hostile internet user against the advertised public TLS hostname. A named human reviewer of this receipt is a separate PUBLIC_LAUNCH obligation (named_reviewer:staging-attack-rehearsal).
gates.reachable_harm_statement: https://mercmerc.net serves public TLS on port 443 with HSTS and answers /buyer, /supplier, /admin, and /prices. A hostile internet user can already reach that hostname, so the executed public-hostname rehearsal is a start-gate of this alpha. The machine checker requires the executed count, per-class results, and public-surface qualification; it does not require a named human.

gates.harm: A machine rehearsal is accepted as the public-surface security bar because it never drove the hostname it names, and nobody is accountable for having looked.
gates.smaller_control: The executed public-hostname rehearsal (attacks_executed, per-class results, surface/qualification/hostname) is independently re-runnable and remains the ALPHA_BLOCKER. Participants are operator-controlled, there is no public signup, and no live money moves.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The named reviewer protects against a paper pass that never drove the surface it names, with nobody accountable for having looked. At backend alpha that harm is bounded: the rehearsal's executed count and per-class results are recorded and independently re-runnable, so a receipt that did not drive mercmerc.net is already refused; participants are operator-controlled, there is no public signup, and no live money moves. At public launch the same harm is not bounded: strangers arrive, and 'a script said it was fine' is not an answer anyone can be held to. Named review of the public-surface rehearsal remains the Level C bar in full.

gates.harm: Double capture, dropped refund, non-idempotent webhook, or ledger/provider disagreement in the money-path logic.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Settlement is in the purpose of this alpha; untested money-path logic will mis-attribute the first test-mode transaction.

gates.harm: The first Stripe test-mode authorization, capture, refund, dispute, Connect hold, or webhook replay disagrees with the ledger because those paths have never spoken to Stripe.
gates.smaller_control: The deterministic simulator covers logic, not the provider contract. There is no smaller substitute for a real sk_test matrix.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: This alpha's purpose includes the money path and settlement; a simulator PASS is not Stripe. The first controlled money-path transaction will hit test-mode Stripe, so the matrix is a start-gate. Live mode stays prohibited.

gates.harm: Lost attempt fencing or unaudited emergency mutation of in-flight jobs, producing duplicate task effects or an unrecoverable lock.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Concurrent claim/fail/commit on a live plane is how this alpha runs work; fencing and audited break-glass are reachable-harm controls, not ceremony.

gates.harm: A process restart loses in-flight jobs or duplicates financial effects.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Machines restart. An alpha that cannot survive a seeded restart-storm without losing work or double-settling will do exactly that on the droplet.

gates.harm: Cannot decrypt and restore the artifact envelope and object store after a local failure, so job outputs and sentinels are gone.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The alpha writes artifacts. If the restore tool has never reconstituted them, the first disk fault ends the experiment's outputs.

gates.harm: A single-provider or single-credential wipe destroys the only copy of the ledger and object ciphertext.
gates.smaller_control: Local encrypted-envelope restore proves the tool. It does not prove that a copy survived leaving the box.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: One droplet, one MinIO, one operator credential. `docker compose down -v` or a disk death is reachable today. A backup that has never left the box is not a backup of the experiment's ledger.

gates.harm: Admitting work onto hardware that cannot run it, or that produces uncharacterized output, so jobs fail or settle on garbage.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: This alpha's purpose is real execution. Uncharacterized Metal/runtime pairs will fail or lie on the first job.

gates.harm: Cannot restore the ledger database after local failure, so settlement state is unrecoverable.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The money path writes Postgres. A restore tool that has never reconstituted the ledger cannot recover the first alpha transaction.

gates.harm: A bad candidate cannot be rolled back; the plane is stuck on a broken digest or a half-applied migration.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: This alpha deploys a real candidate onto persistent state. Without a proven rollback the first bad digest is permanent.

gates.harm: The bytes that left the box are truncated, wrong-key, or unrestorable, and that is discovered only after the primary is gone.
gates.smaller_control: Checksumming an offsite object without restoring it is false comfort. Local restore of local bytes does not prove the offsite bytes.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: A restore path unproven at alpha is a restore path unproven when the droplet is gone. Recovery is in the purpose; the offsite copy must have been reconstituted, not merely uploaded.

gates.harm: The compose/image/scaffold cannot actually boot the candidate (wrong image pin, live Stripe wired, missing service), so 'deployed' is a paper claim.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: A backend alpha that cannot validate its own staging scaffold will boot the wrong thing, or refuse to boot, on the persistent plane.

gates.harm: Cannot swap the control image back to the retained prior digest without losing the data plane.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Persistent Postgres/MinIO plus a bad control digest is the failure mode of this alpha; rollback must have been done, not planned.

gates.harm: A multi-component restart on the deployed shape loses work or duplicates money.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The droplet will be restarted. The seeded storm is the proof that this alpha's shape survives it.

gates.harm: A process that dies or OOMs in the first minute is treated as a viable alpha host.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The 60-second local soak is a witness, not a duration argument. It applies during alpha as a smoke control; the derived 3600 s soak is the start-gate.

gates.harm: A slow leak, a once-per-day timer, or an unattended overnight failure that a short soak would miss — as an *arbitrary 24-hour calendar bar*.
gates.smaller_control: A 3600-second soak derived from pgx MaxConnLifetime=30m (twice the lifetime, so a live pool recycle is observed). Lease expiry, envelope expiry, backup, and payout-hold each have a shorter or on-demand observation path. See docs/BACKEND_ALPHA_CONTRACT.md §6.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: No soak assertion is 24-hour-only. Inflight lease is 30s, verification lease 5m, worker liveness ≤90s, pool recycle 30m, backup is on-demand, envelope min TTL is 30s, payout hold is live-money and unit-tested, chargeBatchMaxAge is tested with aged rows. The 24-hour number is a Level B endurance bar, kept in full there, not the only way to observe a named mechanism on this alpha.

gates.harm: An endurance requirement asserted as a duration nobody derived, so either a real time-dependent mechanism goes unobserved or an arbitrary wait is mistaken for evidence.
gates.smaller_control: Inventory every time-dependent mechanism, state its production period, and exercise each deterministically; record the derivation as a zero-point row.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: This row awards no points and cannot substitute for the 24-hour gate at evidence/external/qualifying-soak-24h.json, which stays unearned. It exists so the soak requirement is a derivation from named mechanisms rather than a number, and so any receipt claiming a 24h wall-clock pass here is refused.

gates.harm: A real failure mode (stuck job, expired lease, webhook dead-letter) never fires an alert, so the supervising operator cannot see it.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The operator is the on-call. If the pipeline cannot fire, the alpha burns silently. That is reachable on day one.

gates.harm: The paging path is miswired, so a firing alert never becomes a human-visible page.
gates.smaller_control: The observed Alertmanager fire/resolve delivery receipt (alert-delivery-r1) is the smaller live control.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: A simulated page is useful during alpha; the live fire/resolve receipt is the start-gate. Staffed vendor paging is a later obligation.

gates.harm: An alert fires and is never observed at a sink, so the supervising operator does not learn the plane is on fire.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: This is the smaller control that replaces staffed 24/7 paging for a supervised alpha. The reachable harm is a silent fire, not an unpaged 03:00 vendor gap.

gates.harm: Cannot export or delete a participant's data, or a restore silently undeletes a tombstone, so a known person cannot leave and their data reappears.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Controlled participants have emails and may have Stripe test-mode customer objects. If DSAR/deletion/tombstone does not work, their data cannot be removed. That is reachable without a public population.

gates.harm: Processing a public population's personal data without a qualified privacy authority, or being unable to delete it from a subprocessor, producing unlawful processing at scale.
gates.smaller_control: Technical DSAR, deletion, and tombstone replay (already scored). No public signup, no broad population.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: There is no public population and no unsupported compliance claim. The harm a counsel signature and subprocessor-deletion exercise prevent is mass unlawful processing, which this alpha cannot reach. The technical deletion path stays an alpha blocker.

gates.harm: Running an unsigned or unattested image whose contents cannot be named, so a license-contaminated or substituted binary executes.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Private execution does not make an unsigned image safe. The SBOM/signature/attestation is the control; the qualified public-distribution approval is a different gate.

gates.harm: Publishing hashes, weights, or assets to strangers without a named licensing authority, so uncleared work is distributed.
gates.smaller_control: In-repo SBOM, digest-pinned images, and the asset-provenance register. Serving the buyer workspace is not public distribution of hashes, weights, or licensed assets.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: This alpha does not publish hashes, weights, or licensed assets to strangers. A public buyer page is not that distribution, so the named licensing-authority harm cannot occur. Running the control plane still needs the signed SBOM, which is a separate alpha blocker.

gates.harm: The operator does not know how to pause intake, revoke a token, or handle a support/security incident when a known participant misbehaves.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: A known participant can still submit something they should not. The technical tabletop plus kill switch and revocation are the reachable-harm controls; a staffed T&S desk is not.

gates.harm: Strangers arrive via public signup and abuse the marketplace (spam, illegal content, payment fraud, multi-account) with no staffed human route.
gates.smaller_control: Operator-as-route, kill switch, credential revocation, admission policy, and the passing technical tabletops.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: There is no public signup and no anonymous population. The abuse a staffed T&S desk exists to absorb cannot arrive. A known participant is handled by the operator and the technical controls.

gates.harm: A settlement/display mismatch is 'fixed' off-ledger because the operator has never walked the support path.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The operator will be the support desk. The technical tabletop already proves they can reconcile to the immutable ledger. Named 24/7 coverage is a later org.

gates.harm: A public buyer cannot complete the website flow, or the site leaks credentials, or it fails accessibility — against a shipped consumer website.
gates.smaller_control: None. The buyer workspace is served on public TLS; there is no smaller substitute for validating that page.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: https://mercmerc.net/buyer is a public HTML buyer workspace with Stripe.js in the CSP, and /supplier, /admin, and /prices answer too. A broken, leaky, or inaccessible buyer flow is a reachable start-gate harm on the shipped site.

gates.harm: The live process never survives a pgx pool recycle (MaxConnLifetime=30m) or a handful of verification-lease and worker-liveness cycles, so the alpha dies mid-experiment after looking healthy for minutes.
gates.smaller_control: Local 60s/300s/900s soaks do not reach MaxConnLifetime. Unit tests do not recycle the production pool.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Twice MaxConnLifetime (3600s) is the shortest duration that observes a live pool recycle with samples on both sides. That mechanism is in the running control plane and is not 24-hour-only. The 24-hour receipt remains the Level B bar.

gates.harm: Calling the backend ready when no persistent control + data plane exists, so the first transaction runs against a laptop compose or nothing.
gates.smaller_control: Health, auth, storage, and lifecycle probes against the persistent plane. That plane is the advertised public TLS hostname mercmerc.net.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: This alpha is a deployed backend. Without a persistent plane there is nothing to transact against. The plane that exists serves public TLS on mercmerc.net and answers buyer routes; persistence remains this P1's start-gate, and the public hostname is the attack surface of the security rehearsal gate.

gates.harm: A bad digest cannot be rolled back, a restart-storm loses work, or the live process has never been watched across a pool-recycle window.
gates.smaller_control: The 24-hour clause is not the only observation of those harms. Alpha exit is rollback + restart-storm on the persistent plane plus the 3600s derived soak. The 24-hour qualifying property stays the Level B bar in full.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Rollback, restart, and a mechanism-derived soak are reachable-harm start-gates. The arbitrary 86400s duration is not; it remains owned by Level B. See soak:alpha-derived and docs/BACKEND_ALPHA_CONTRACT.md §6.
gates.alpha_exit_criterion: Run rollback/forward of the exact candidate against the persistent data plane, preserve a seeded restart-storm receipt, and complete a qualifying soak of at least 3600 seconds (2× MaxConnLifetime) with the same hold-still assertions. The 24-hour window remains the Level B/C exit criterion of this same P1.

gates.harm: Irrecoverable loss of the experiment's ledger and objects after a single-box or single-credential wipe, because ciphertext never crossed an independent boundary or was never restored from that copy.
gates.smaller_control: Local encrypted restore proves the tool. It does not prove the off-box bytes exist or restore.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Disagree with the prior Level-C-only scoping. Recovery is in the purpose. One droplet wipe is reachable. A restore path unproven at alpha is unproven when it matters. The full independent-boundary restore stays the gate; it is not replaced by 'we can re-seed synthetics'.

gates.harm: The first test-mode charge, refund, dispute, Connect hold, or webhook disagrees with the ledger because Stripe test mode has never been exercised.
gates.smaller_control: The 4096-sequence simulator is not Stripe.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Settlement is in the purpose. Live mode stays prohibited. The test-mode matrix is the start-gate for the money path this alpha exists to exercise.

gates.harm: A production incident fires at 03:00 and never pages a staffed human on a vendor acknowledgement route.
gates.smaller_control: Observed Alertmanager → HTTP sink fire/resolve receipt (alert-delivery-r1), already passing. The operator supervises this alpha in person.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Unattended 24/7 vendor paging is the harm. This alpha is supervised. The reachable silent-fire harm is already protected by the local delivery receipt. The staffed PagerDuty/Opsgenie route remains the Level C bar in full.

gates.harm: The buyer/supplier/execution/verification/settlement paths have never been driven end to end, so 'the backend works' is a unit-test claim.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The counted matrix is the engineering rehearsal — it is how the alpha begins, not a paper precondition of beginning. Completing it with two synthetic buyers and two operator Metal workers must not, and cannot, flip EXTERNAL_ALPHA_PROVEN.

gates.harm: The author self-approves a closure PR that authorizes irreversible third-party harm (real charges, public access, independent suppliers).
gates.smaller_control: Machine receipts scored by validate-readiness.py. Live money and public launch stay NO_GO_PROHIBITED regardless of who merges.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: Self-merging ALPHA_ENGINEERING_READY cannot charge the public or enroll independent suppliers. The irreversible-third-party-harm approval remains the Level C bar in full.

gates.harm: Operating a public or live-money service without qualified security, privacy, legal, licensing, payments, operations, supplier-policy, and release approvals, plus named human incident coverage.
gates.smaller_control: Technical DSAR, technical tabletops, operator supervision, and the containment that live money and public signup stay prohibited.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: A production-scale legal program and a staffed coverage roster are excluded from this alpha by contract. Each named harm is either absent (no public counterparty, no live charges, no mass PII) or independently prohibited. The eight-approval bundle remains the Level C bar in full.

gates.harm: Independently owned supplier hardware receives and retains buyer input without contract, verified location, destination-pinned egress, confidentiality, or attestation.
gates.smaller_control: The control is the prohibition itself. Operator-controlled devices are permitted for ALPHA_ENGINEERING_READY.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The harm is reachable the moment an uncontrolled GPU is enrolled. The prohibition must stay in force for this alpha (ALPHA_BLOCKER as containment). The expansion exit criteria remain the Level C / POST_ALPHA bar in full and are also required before EXTERNAL_ALPHA_PROVEN can be GO.
gates.note: Classification applies to keeping the prohibition in force. The expansion_exit_criterion is not closeable as an alpha PASS.

gates.harm: Reporting that an independent external buyer and supplier have used the system when only synthetics or the operator's own devices have.
gates.reachable_harm_statement: The engineering rehearsal is defined on synthetic buyers and operator Metal workers. Counting those identities as independent externals is a false claim, not a later-level concern. The checker refuses every synthetic marker and demands per-supplier P0 expansion fields before the claim can be GO.
